audience: Python developers building long-lived agents whose memory holds facts that change (plans, employers, addresses), and who are deciding right now how an update should supersede the old value
other_audiences: mem0 users hitting conflicting memories after ADD-only extraction (launch.json A2)
Teams building domain apps (research, legal, engineering design) that want a typed schema and declared conflict rules for memory
Non-Python services that want typed memory over HTTP/TypeScript (states are not exposed there yet)

problem.text: Facts an agent relies on change, arrive late, or come from sources that disagree; a memory that overwrites or appends can't say which value is current.

capabilities.name: set / get / history: one current value per named state, earlier values kept
Order values by validity time (valid_from/valid_to), not arrival order
Point-in-time reads: get/history as_of a date; scheduled values
StateConflict: same-moment or weaker-later disagreement has no current value
Sources with authority on every value; repeats add a source
typedmem set / get / history CLI (get exits 3 on conflict)
Local SQLite / JSONL stores that persist states and their history
Zero runtime dependencies (stdlib only; extras opt-in)
Replayable event log with before/after snapshots
Typed memory: DomainProfile schemas and per-type ConflictPolicy
Evolvers: preference drift, goal resolution, non-destructive summaries
Transition kernel: one write funnel with optimistic concurrency (provisional API)
Semantic recall over stored memories (hashing embedder default)
HTTP server and TypeScript client for typed memory (not states)

values.outcome: Know which value is current when a fact changes, without losing the values it had before
values.why: The agent doesn't act on a stale value, and can still answer questions about what used to be true

proof.claim: All 53 state acceptance tests pass across in-memory, JSONL and SQLite stores
The README's set/get/history transcript runs and its output matches the README exactly

Recorded external run at reliagent-bench@df0ebc6 (read from its committed result file, not re-executed): LongMemEval knowledge-update, states 65/65 vs typed REPLACE 54/65; history questions 11/11 vs 0/11

values.outcome: A late record about the past goes into history instead of overwriting the present
values.why: An old support ticket or re-ingested document can't silently roll the agent back

proof.claim: OpenAI → Anthropic, then a late Google (2022) lands in history; get stays Anthropic

values.outcome: Ask what a value was on any past date, or schedule one for the future
values.why: Questions like 'what plan were they on in April?' get the value valid then, not the latest

proof.claim: as_of returns the value valid at that date; ended and scheduled values handled

values.outcome: When sources genuinely disagree, get an explicit conflict instead of a guessed current value
values.why: The agent doesn't confidently act on one side of an unresolved disagreement; you see both values and their sources

proof.claim: Simultaneous and weaker-later disagreements raise StateConflict; a stronger later value resolves it
The README conflict transcript (get exits 3, both values shown with sources) runs and matches

values.caveat: Measured cost (reliagent-bench df0ebc6, external/results/states-0.9.3.md): against a Mode A gold that expects silent authority vetoes, states score authority 0.50 vs typed-memory 1.00, because they report a conflict instead

values.outcome: See where every value came from, and let a trusted source outrank an agent's own guess
values.why: You can debug why the agent believes something, and a low-authority inference can't silently override what the user said

proof.claim: Repeating a value adds its source without a new history entry
A later but weaker value opens a conflict; a later stronger one supersedes

values.outcome: Rebuild and audit exactly how the agent's memory reached its current state
values.why: When memory is wrong you can prove what changed, when and from which source, and replay it

proof.claim: The event log replays to exactly the stored state, including state changes

values.outcome: Keep the agent's state in a local file you own; it survives restarts with its history and conflicts intact
values.why: Safe to adopt: no service to run, no hosted memory cloud

proof.claim: History, conflicts and replay survive close/reopen for JSONL and SQLite

values.outcome: Install it without pulling in any other package
values.why: Nothing to vet or conflict with in an existing agent stack

proof.claim: dependencies = [] in pyproject (the local .venv metadata is a stale 0.9.1 install, so it was not used as proof)

values.outcome: Declare per-type rules for domain memory: reject invalid writes, supersede decisions, merge corroborating sources, flag contradictions
values.why: For domain apps where 'the memory accepted nonsense' is a correctness bug, and where a policy should pick a winner

proof.claim: Policy, profile and schema tests pass
Contradiction surfacing and authority guard tests pass

values.outcome: Use typed memory from non-Python services over HTTP
values.why: A TypeScript or other service can share the same memory store

proof.claim: Server endpoints (add/get/list/recall/history/timeline/contradictions, 422 on profile rejection) pass

values.outcome: Find relevant stored memories by meaning, weighted by recency and confidence
values.why: The agent can pull the memories that matter for a question without an external vector DB

lead_reason.relevance: Answers P1, the strongest observed pain (the old fact and its replacement both come back and the agent has to guess), and P2 (people want a validity window and history, not an overwrite)

differentiation.alternative: a memory layer that overwrites on update (REPLACE / UPDATE) or appends every version and leaves the agent to pick
differentiation.why: Keeps every value and says which one is current by validity time, so a late old record can't overwrite the present; measured 11/11 vs 0/11 history questions against REPLACE. Honest limit: it only ties keep-both and bitemporal baselines on those runs, and the launch evidence shows several Show HN projects already offer bi-temporal/supersede memory, so the edge is the small set/get/history contract plus refusing to guess (V2), not validity time alone

advanced.reason: Real and tested (V6), answers P4 partially, but the owner chose state-first; keep under Advanced
Trust value (V4) with no observed pain; say it, don't lead with it
Serves typed memory only; states are Python/CLI, so leading with it would mislead the audience
Commodity every alternative offers; README itself says TypedMem does not compete on retrieval
Drift, goal resolution and summaries: no mapped value in this map and no observed pain
Internal write funnel; the API is provisional until v1.0
